items.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015
items.q: Bob was teacher to Eddie Palmieri... I learned about permutations... But I never took like Theory 101

ctx.x: Oh my, I’ve heard that word a lot.

Yeah. And Bob was teacher to Eddie Palmieri, to Michael Brecker, to Randy Brecker, and he also taught economics from his home. He was quite, quite a man, a really eccentric man, and I miss him deeply. Tim [Hauser] also studied with Bob. So that opened up the world of sigma and thirteenth chords, and I learned about permutations, permuting melody, permuting rhythms, it’s very intellectual though. I found it very intellectual. But I never took like Theory 101 so I’m like there were major like holes in my musical…
Transfer,” I arranged “Candy,” I arranged — what else did I arrange — oh “You Can Depend on Me” probably. But it was by ear.
